faq: Where do the test questions come from?

Mostly from you: past chats, support emails and search logs. If you have little, we write realistic questions with you and add tricky ones. We never use real customers' personal details in the report.
Can you test without seeing customer data?
Yes. You can strip names and emails first, or give us only the question text. We only need the wording of each question and, if possible, the answer you would want.
Will you change my AI tool?
Only the parts you allow, usually its instructions, settings or source content. We list every change and keep the old version so you can go back.
Do you test voice or images?
Text is the default. Image questions can be tested if your tool accepts pictures. Voice tools are tested through their written transcript. Tell us what you use in the form.

desc:
AI answer testing and quality review shows how your AI tool performs on real questions, scored for accuracy, tone and safety. Ecom Swift LLC runs the tests, explains where answers go wrong, fixes what we can and leaves you a test set you can run again.

## What is AI answer testing?

It is a structured check of an AI tool using the kinds of questions real people ask. Each question is run through the tool, and a reviewer scores the answer against a clear standard: is it correct, is it in the right tone, is it safe and does it stay on topic. The scores are collected into a report.

This replaces the usual informal approach of trying a few questions and deciding that it seems fine. A few lucky answers say little about the hundreds that follow.

## Why spot checks are not enough

AI tools fail in uneven ways. They may handle common questions well and still stumble on a rare product, an unusual phrasing or a question that mixes two topics. A change to instructions or content that improves one answer can quietly worsen another.

Without a test set, nobody knows whether last week's change helped or hurt. With one, you can run the same questions again and compare.

## How review improves your tool

Testing finds problems before customers do. A wrong delivery policy, a rude tone or a reply that invents a feature is far cheaper to fix in a test than after it has been seen publicly.

The fixes are usually practical: clearer instructions, a missing document added to the source, a setting adjusted or a topic restricted. We report the patterns behind failures, so you can tell whether the cause is the tool, the content or the question. Scores describe what we tested, not every possible conversation.

## What a good review includes

- Real questions collected from customers, staff, emails and chat logs.
- A written scoring guide, so judgments are consistent.
- Separate scores for accuracy, tone and safety.
- Edge cases, such as vague questions, mixed topics and attempts to go off topic.
- A list of weak spots, grouped into patterns.
- Fixes to instructions, settings or content, with notes on each change.
- Before and after scores for the questions that were fixed.
- A list of content gaps for your team to fill.
- A reusable test sheet in a spreadsheet.
- A walkthrough of findings in plain words.

## What we do

We collect questions with you, or write realistic ones if customer data is sensitive. We run each through your tool and score the replies. Then we group the failures, make the fixes that are within the tool's settings and instructions, and re-test the affected answers.

The Basic package scores a set of real questions and lists weak spots. The Standard package covers a larger set, makes fixes, shows before and after scores, names the top problem patterns and re-tests. The Premium package adds edge cases, a content gaps list, a reusable test sheet, fixes across two tools and a walkthrough call. We change your tool only within what you approve, and we keep notes so changes can be reversed.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Include questions that real customers found confusing.
- Keep the test set after the review and run it before every change.
- Score answers the same way each time.
- Pass content gaps to the person who owns that content.
- Test again after fixes rather than assuming they worked.

**Avoid:**
- Testing only questions you already know the tool handles.
- Judging a tool by its best answer instead of its worst.
- Changing several things at once, then not knowing which one helped.
- Using the test questions as training examples and then re-testing on the same ones.
- Treating a good score as permission to stop monitoring.

## Who it is for

A store owner runs a shopping assistant and wants evidence that it answers correctly. A support manager is considering an AI reply tool and needs a fair test before committing. A team about to change its instructions wants a baseline to compare against.

## What we need from you

We need access to the tool, either as a test link or as a collaborator or team user, and any real questions you can share with private details removed. If you cannot share customer data, we write realistic questions with you. We never need passwords. Voice and image tools can be tested when we agree the method first.
